item.title: [BM] Dzulkefly Janji — Sekali Lagi — Nak Banteras Buli Tempat Kerja Di Hospital Kerajaan
item.description:
Said by: Dzulkefly Ahmad, Health Minister

Category: Health

Date: 2026-03-10

📌 Apa Yang Berlaku

Menteri Kesihatan Dzulkefly Ahmad mengumumkan pada 10 Mac 2026 bahawa Kementerian Kesihatan akan “memperkukuh penguatkuasaan” terhadap buli tempat kerja di kemudahan kesihatan kerajaan. Beliau berkata hospital awam sepatutnya menjadi “persekitaran kerja yang profesional dan beretika” dan merujuk kepada pekeliling Jabatan Perkhidmatan Awam (JPA) yang melarang bahasa kasar dan penderaan lisan di tempat kerja. Beliau berjanji untuk “mempertingkatkan pelaksanaan” pekeliling tersebut.

item.title: Dzulkefly Promises — Again — to Crack Down on Workplace Bullying in Government Hospitals
item.description:
Said by: Dzulkefly Ahmad, Health Minister

Category: Health

Date: 2026-03-10

📌 What Happened

Health Minister Dzulkefly Ahmad announced on March 10, 2026 that the Health Ministry will “bolster enforcement” against workplace bullying in government health facilities. He said public hospitals should be “professional and ethical workplace environments” and pointed to a Public Services Department (PSD) circular that bans coarse language and verbal abuse in the workplace. He pledged to “enhance implementation” of the circular to ensure “no ambiguity” in handling misconduct — language that strongly implies the existing rules are not being enforced.

item.title: [BM] Doktor Kontrak: 33,000 MASIH Menunggu Jawatan Tetap — Janji Dibuat Pada 2020, Masih Dimungkiri Pada 2026
item.description:
Said by: Malaysian Medical Association / Contract Doctors

Category: Health

Date: 2026-01-01

📌 APA YANG BERLAKU: Sehingga Januari 2026, kira-kira 33,000 doktor kontrak dalam sistem penjagaan kesihatan awam Malaysia terus bekerja dengan kontrak sementara tanpa jaminan pekerjaan, faedah pencen, atau laluan kemajuan kerjaya yang tersedia untuk pegawai perubatan tetap. Sistem kontrak diperkenalkan sebagai langkah “sementara” untuk menyerap lonjakan graduan perubatan. Enam tahun kemudian, ia masih “sementara.” Doktor kontrak melakukan kerja yang sama dengan doktor tetap — mereka melihat pesakit yang sama, bekerja minggu 84 jam yang sama, mengendalikan kecemasan yang sama — tetapi tanpa status pekerjaan tetap. CNA melaporkan mengenai krisis “kekurangan doktor, gaji rendah, minggu kerja 84 jam.” P4H Network menggambarkan sistem penjagaan kesihatan Malaysia sebagai “bom jangka.”

item.title: Contract Doctors: 33,000 STILL Waiting for Permanent Posts — Promise Made in 2020, Still Broken in 2026
item.description:
Said by: Malaysian Medical Association / Contract Doctors

Category: Health

Date: 2026-01-01

📌 WHAT HAPPENED: As of January 2026, approximately 33,000 contract doctors in Malaysia’s public healthcare system continue to work on temporary contracts without job security, pension benefits, or career advancement pathways available to permanent medical officers. The contract system was introduced as a “temporary” measure to absorb a surge of medical graduates. Six years later, it is still “temporary.” Contract doctors do the same work as permanent doctors — they see the same patients, work the same 84-hour weeks, handle the same emergencies — but without permanent employment status. CNA reported on the “doctor shortage, low pay, 84-hour working week” crisis. P4H Network described Malaysia’s healthcare system as a “ticking bomb.”

item.title: [BM] Keluarga T20 Kini Guna Hospital Kerajaan — Golongan Kaya Pun Tak Mampu Penjagaan Kesihatan Swasta
item.description:
Said by: Federation of Malaysian Consumers Associations / The Star

Category: Health

Date: 2025-09-08

📌 Apa Yang Berlaku

Gabungan Persatuan-Persatuan Pengguna Malaysia (FOMCA) membunyikan penggera bahawa malah keluarga T20 (20% berpendapatan tertinggi) kini beralih ke hospital kerajaan kerana penjagaan kesihatan swasta menjadi terlalu mahal. Pengurus kanan FOMCA Saral James Maniam memanggilnya ‘bendera merah besar.’

🔥 Mengapa Ia Penting

Apabila rakyat Malaysia terkaya mendapati penjagaan kesihatan swasta tidak mampu dibayar, keseluruhan model pembiayaan penjagaan kesihatan telah runtuh. Keluarga-keluarga ini membanjiri hospital kerajaan yang sudah terbeban, mewujudkan barisan lebih panjang dan hasil lebih buruk untuk pesakit B40 dan M40 yang tiada alternatif. Sistem ini mengalami gelung kemusnahan: kos swasta meningkat → T20 beralih ke awam → sistem awam terbeban → kualiti merosot → tiada siapa mendapat penjagaan memadai.

item.title: [BM] Sistem Penjagaan Kesihatan Malaysia: 'Bom Jangka' — 2.83% KDNK Sementara Negara Lain Belanja Dua Kali Ganda
item.description:
Said by: P4H Network / University of Malaya Working Paper / The Star

Category: Health

Date: 2025-09-08

📌 Apa Yang Berlaku

Pelbagai analisis bebas telah mengisytiharkan sistem penjagaan kesihatan Malaysia sebagai ‘bom jangka.’ Perbelanjaan kesihatan awam hanya pada 2.83% KDNK pada 2023, jauh di bawah paras yang disyorkan WHO dan rakan serantau. Nisbah doktor-pesakit 1:417 menyembunyikan krisis sebenar di sektor awam, yang mengendalikan 80% katil hospital dengan 54% doktor. Negara ini kekurangan 11,000 pakar. Doktor muda bekerja 84 jam seminggu.

item.title: Malaysia's Healthcare System: A 'Ticking Bomb' — 2.83% of GDP While Countries Spend Double
item.description:
Said by: P4H Network / University of Malaya Working Paper / The Star

Category: Health

Date: 2025-09-08

📌 What Happened

Multiple independent analyses have declared Malaysia’s healthcare system a ’ticking bomb.’ Public health expenditure sits at just 2.83% of GDP in 2023, far below WHO-recommended levels and regional peers. The doctor-to-patient ratio of 1:417 masks the true crisis in the public sector, which handles 80% of hospital beds with 54% of doctors. The country is 11,000 specialists short. Junior doctors work 84-hour weeks.

item.title: T20 Families Now Using Public Hospitals — The Rich Can't Afford Private Healthcare Anymore
item.description:
Said by: Federation of Malaysian Consumers Associations / The Star

Category: Health

Date: 2025-09-08

📌 What Happened

The Federation of Malaysian Consumers Associations (FOMCA) sounded alarms that even T20 families (top 20% income earners) are switching to public hospitals because private healthcare has become prohibitively expensive. FOMCA senior manager Saral James Maniam called it a ‘big red flag.’

🔥 Why It Matters

When Malaysia’s wealthiest citizens find private healthcare unaffordable, the entire healthcare financing model has collapsed. These families flood already-overwhelmed public hospitals, creating longer queues and worse outcomes for B40 and M40 patients who have no alternative. The system is experiencing a doom loop: rising private costs → T20 shift to public → public system overwhelmed → quality drops → nobody gets adequate care.

item.title: [BM] Krisis K-Pod Dan Vape Dalam Kalangan Belia — Wabak Dadah Baru Sementara Kerajaan Lambat Bertindak
item.description:
Said by: DPM Ahmad Zahid / AADK

Category: Health

Date: 2025-08-10

📌 Apa Yang Berlaku

Krisis dadah baru yang dahsyat sedang melanda sekolah dan komuniti Malaysia: K-pod dan vape berlapis dadah sintetik menjadi mekanisme penghantaran dadah pilihan belia Malaysia. Timbalan PM Ahmad Zahid mengakui keadaan berada pada ’tahap kritikal,’ dengan kes penyalahgunaan dadah melonjak 32.5% dari 2023 ke 2024 dan perangsang jenis amfetamina terlibat dalam lebih 70% kes.

🔥 Mengapa Ia Penting

Fenomena K-pod — kartrij vape berlapis dadah sintetik — amat berbahaya kerana ia menyamarkan penggunaan dadah sebagai vape biasa, menjadikan pengesanan oleh ibu bapa dan guru hampir mustahil. Platform media sosial telah menjadi saluran pengedaran, dengan pengedar mengiklan melalui Telegram dan TikTok.

item.title: K-Pods and Vape Crisis Among Youth — New Drug Epidemic While Government Plays Catch-Up
item.description:
Said by: DPM Ahmad Zahid / AADK

Category: Health

Date: 2025-08-10

📌 What Happened

A devastating new drug crisis is sweeping through Malaysian schools and communities: K-pods and synthetic drug-laced vapes are becoming the drug delivery mechanism of choice for young Malaysians. Deputy PM Ahmad Zahid acknowledged the situation was at a ‘critical level,’ with drug abuse cases surging 32.5% from 2023 to 2024 and amphetamine-type stimulants involved in over 70% of cases.

item.title: [BM] Krisis Doktor Kontrak: Ribuan Letak Jawatan Kerana Kerajaan Mungkiri Janji Jawatan Tetap
item.description:
Said by: Malaysian Medical Association and contract doctors

Category: Health

Date: 2025-07-28

Doktor-Doktor Sedang Pergi

Menjelang pertengahan 2025, sistem penjagaan kesihatan Malaysia diisytiharkan “dalam keadaan kritikal” oleh FMT. Krisis doktor kontrak — bom jangka yang PH warisi dan janji untuk diselesaikan — semakin teruk sahaja.

Fakta-Fakta

Fakta: Antara 2022 dan 2024, 705 doktor dan 1,394 jururawat dengan lebih lima tahun perkhidmatan meletak jawatan daripada hospital kerajaan.

Fakta: Persatuan Perubatan Malaysia menyeru pemansuhan sepenuhnya sistem kontrak, yang mengunci doktor dalam kontrak 3+2+2+4 tahun tanpa jaminan pekerjaan.

item.title: Contract Doctors Crisis: Thousands Resign as Government Breaks Promise on Permanent Posts
item.description:
Said by: Malaysian Medical Association and contract doctors

Category: Health

Date: 2025-07-28

The Doctors Are Leaving

By mid-2025, Malaysia’s healthcare system was declared “in critical condition” by FMT. The contract doctor crisis — a ticking bomb PH inherited and promised to fix — had only gotten worse.

The Facts

Fact: Between 2022 and 2024, 705 doctors and 1,394 nurses with over five years of service resigned from public hospitals.

Fact: The Malaysian Medical Association called for the complete abolition of the contract system, which locks doctors into 3+2+2+4 year contracts with no job security.

item.title: [BM] Rekod 236 Tan Syabu Dirampas Di Rantau — Malaysia Hab Transit Utama
item.description:
Said by: UNODC Report 2025

Category: Health

Date: 2025-05-28

UNODC reported a record 236 tons of methamphetamine seized in East and Southeast Asia in 2024, up 24% from 2023. Malaysia busted its largest-ever maritime drug trafficking ring — 18+ tonnes worth RM375M. Drug use is increasing among older demographics. Government approved a ‘communication plan’ — not enforcement reform. This matters because Malaysia abolished mandatory death for drug trafficking, then watched seizures hit record highs. The government’s response to a worsening drug crisis was a ‘communication plan’ — essentially a PR strategy instead of structural enforcement reform. Malaysia sits on a major trafficking corridor and its ports are clearly being exploited. Record seizures can mean better enforcement or a bigger problem — and when the UNODC says the regional supply is surging 24% year-on-year, it’s the latter. A government that responds to a drug tsunami with a communications strategy is not serious about the problem. Sources: UNODC | Vietnam Plus

item.title: [BM] Hospital Awam Kekurangan 11,000 Pakar — Hanya 14 Pakar Bedah Kardiotoraks Seluruh Negara
item.description:
Said by: Health Ministry Data

Category: Health

Date: 2025-04-01

📌 Apa Yang Berlaku

Malaysia hanya mempunyai 14 pakar bedah kardiotoraks merentasi 7 hospital awam, dan hospital awam kekurangan hampir 11,000 doktor pakar keseluruhannya. Apabila seorang profesor UiTM mencadangkan membuka program perubatan khusus Bumiputera kepada pelajar Cina dan India sebagai langkah sementara, ahli politik Melayu menyerang idea itu.

🔥 Mengapa Ia Penting

Orang secara literal mati kerana dasar kaum mengatasi keperluan perubatan. Kekurangan pakar bukan masalah kakitangan — ia adalah pilihan dasar. Malaysia menyekat siapa boleh berlatih di institusi tertentu berdasarkan etnik, kemudian tertanya mengapa tidak cukup pakar.

item.title: Public Hospitals Short 11,000 Specialists — Only 14 Cardiothoracic Surgeons Nationwide
item.description:
Said by: Health Ministry Data

Category: Health

Date: 2025-04-01

📌 What Happened

Malaysia has only 14 cardiothoracic surgeons across 7 public hospitals, and public hospitals are short nearly 11,000 specialist doctors overall. When a UiTM professor suggested opening the Bumiputera-only medical program to Chinese and Indian students as a stopgap, Malay politicians attacked the idea.

🔥 Why It Matters

People are literally dying because race policy trumps medical need. The specialist shortage is not a staffing problem — it is a policy choice. Malaysia restricts who can train at certain institutions based on ethnicity, then wonders why it doesn’t have enough specialists.

item.title: [BM] Krisis Kesihatan Mental Berputar — Bunuh Diri Dan Kemurungan Belia Melonjak Sementara Kerajaan Kurang Dana Perkhidmatan
item.description:
Said by: Health Ministry / WHO Data

Category: Health

Date: 2025-01-01

📌 Apa Yang Berlaku

Malaysia menghadapi krisis kesihatan mental yang semakin mendalam, terutamanya dalam kalangan orang muda, dengan kadar kemurungan, kebimbangan, dan bunuh diri yang meningkat. Tinjauan Kesihatan dan Morbiditi Kebangsaan secara konsisten menunjukkan peningkatan yang membimbangkan dalam isu kesihatan mental, dengan hampir 3 daripada 10 rakyat Malaysia mengalami sejenis masalah kesihatan mental.

🔥 Mengapa Ia Penting

Belia terjejas secara tidak seimbang: tekanan media sosial, tekanan akademik, ketidaktentuan ekonomi dengan pengangguran belia 12.28%, dan kesan psikologi COVID-19 yang berlarutan telah mewujudkan ribut sempurna. Namun perkhidmatan kesihatan mental kerajaan kekal sangat kurang dana dan kurang kakitangan. Hospital awam menghadapi kekurangan pakar psikiatri dan ahli psikologi yang teruk, dengan masa menunggu berminggu-minggu atau berbulan-bulan.

item.title: Mental Health Crisis Spiralling — Youth Suicide and Depression Surge While Government Underfunds Services
item.description:
Said by: Health Ministry / WHO Data

Category: Health

Date: 2025-01-01

📌 What Happened

Malaysia is facing a deepening mental health crisis, particularly among young people, with rising rates of depression, anxiety, and suicide. The National Health and Morbidity Survey has consistently shown alarming increases in mental health issues, with nearly 3 in 10 Malaysians experiencing some form of mental health problem.

🔥 Why It Matters

Youth are disproportionately affected: social media pressure, academic stress, economic uncertainty with 12.28% youth unemployment, and the COVID-19 pandemic’s lingering psychological effects have created a perfect storm. Yet government mental health services remain woefully underfunded and understaffed. Public hospitals face severe shortages of psychiatrists and psychologists, with waiting times stretching weeks or months.
